newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Goncz signs bill he earlier vetoed.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Goncz signs bill he earlier vetoed.

text.p: Hungarian President Arpad Goncz has signed into law a bill covering conflicts of interest of members of parliament that he had originally vetoed, a Hungarian newspaper reported on Tuesday.

Goncz shocked the governing coalition of Socialists and Free Democrats in January when he vetoed the bill which bans MPs from holding positions in companies with a state-owned stake of over 10 percent.
The daily Nepszabadsag said the president will on Tuesday inform Parliament that he has signed the bill.

He originally rejected the bill on the grounds that it applied only to posts taken up since 1994 elections. The bill was passed by a two thirds majority, and under Hungary's constitution Goncz was obliged to sign it.

He also sent back a set of amendments to the privatisation law which would allow APV, the state privatisation agency, to transfer assets free of charge to municipalities and state-owned co-operatives.
The privatisation amendments had been fiercely attacked by opposition parties on the grounds that such powers would be tantamount to "legalised corruption".
The government returned the bill to Goncz with the co-operatives clause removed.

Any Hungarian citizen, including opposition MPs, will still be entitled to challenge the conflict of interest law before the Constitutional Court but parliamentary leader of the opposition Fidesz party said they would not do so.
"This is not a constitutional question," Joszef Szajer told Reuters. "We will push for a stricter law at a later date."
